acquisitions.title: AWS Weekly Roundup: Welcome DuckLabs to the team, Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD), and more (August 31, 2026)
acquisitions.excerpt: Amazon Web Services has signed a definitive agreement to acquire DuckLabs, the Amsterdam-based company behind the open-source analytical database DuckDB. DuckDB will remain open source under its independent foundation and the MIT licence, with co-founders Hannes Mühleisen and Mark Raasveldt continuing to lead its technical direction. The in-process database executes SQL directly against file formats such as Parquet, CSV and JSON, operating either locally or on Amazon S3. AWS plans to integrate DuckDB's query speed with enterprise-scale services including Amazon Redshift, Amazon Athena, Amazon EMR, AWS Glue and Amazon SageMaker over time. Because the software handles smaller analytical queries efficiently, it pairs effectively with AI agents that experiment and interact with data. Vice President and Distinguished Engineer Andy Warfield discussed the acquisition and analytical trends in a post on the All Things Distributed blog. The update formed part of the weekly roundup published on the official AWS News Blog.

launches.title: Trump unveils his new Super Intelligence Force
launches.excerpt: President Donald Trump has announced the creation of a new Super Intelligence Force to coordinate federal efforts regarding artificial intelligence. Trump stated on social media that the initiative aims to maintain American leadership in super intelligence and protect the interests of citizens. The announcement follows a September commitment by the president to establish an AI force and appoint an AI czar. The administration has recently moved to rebrand artificial intelligence as super intelligence, a term reflected in the name of the new task force. National intelligence director Jay Clayton will chair the organisation, serving as the designated czar. Vice chairs include Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson, Undersecretary of War for Research and Engineering Emil Michael, and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor. The task force has been given 120 days to compile a report detailing the risks and opportunities associated with artificial intelligence. Clayton emphasised that a primary risk for the United States is failing to maintain its leading position globally while other nations advance. According to the group’s charter, the task force will formulate responses to societal threats enabled by super intelligence while avoiding excessive regulation that could hinder innovation.

launches.title: Sanders introduces bill to ban the federal government from using Flock
launches.excerpt: Senator Bernie Sanders has introduced the Ban Flock Act to prevent federal agencies from using automatic licence plate readers or accessing data gathered by systems operated by local police and private companies. Although named after Flock Safety, the legislation applies broadly to all automatic licence plate reader systems rather than mentioning the company directly in its text. The proposed bill permits exceptions exclusively for toll collection and specific uses authorised by future congressional legislation that would restrict data retention to forty-eight hours. State and local governments that failed to comply with the ban would face financial penalties by losing grants from five federal departments, including the Department of Justice and the Department of Homeland Security. Additionally, the legislation would allow citizens to sue the federal government for violations and empower state attorneys general to enforce the rules. According to Sanders, Flock is the largest automatic licence plate reader vendor in the United States, operating more than 120,000 cameras and processing over twenty billion vehicle reads monthly. The company faces mounting public criticism, community protests, and contract cancellations, prompting recent adjustments such as reducing its default data retention period from thirty days to seven days and introducing audit tools for unusual searches. Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Senator Jeff Merkley have joined as co-sponsors of the bill.

launches.title: AWS Health introduces the version catalog for software lifecycle management
launches.excerpt: Amazon Web Services has launched a new version catalog within AWS Health to provide a centralised source of lifecycle information for software versions across its services. This feature is designed to help customers transition from reactive management to a more proactive approach regarding version upgrades and end-of-support risks. The tool is accessible directly through the AWS Health Dashboard. Furthermore, customers subscribed to Business Support Plus, Enterprise Support, or Unified Operations can utilise the AWS Health API to integrate this lifecycle data into their existing operational workflows. Maintaining currency with software versions is essential for users running applications on the cloud platform to ensure a strong security and operational posture. While AWS Health previously sent account and resource-specific planned lifecycle events well in advance of major version expirations, the new catalogue introduces a service-wide view of supported versions and their respective timelines. This broader visibility enables users to construct effective upgrade schedules and governance controls, allowing them to migrate to newer supported software before receiving direct, account-specific notifications. At launch, the catalogue supports multiple AWS services, including Amazon RDS, Amazon EKS, and AWS Lambda, with plans to incorporate additional services over time. The new functionality is currently available across all AWS Commercial Regions for eligible users.

launches.title: US military ends long-running program to spot nuclear missile launches
launches.excerpt: The United States military has officially retired the long-running Defense Support Program, which used infrared satellite technology to detect nuclear missile launches for more than five decades. The program began in November 1970 when a Titan IIIC rocket carried the first top-secret payload into geosynchronous orbit from Cape Canaveral. These early satellites functioned as sensitive telescopes equipped with infrared detectors designed to continuously monitor the globe and serve as a primary element of Cold War deterrence. Over subsequent decades, the constellation expanded in size, mass and capability, with later iterations featuring thousands of detectors and launching on various vehicles, including a 1991 space shuttle mission. Although the final two surviving satellites continued flying operationally until recently, independent orbital tracking and a US Space Force statement confirmed they raised their orbits in September to enter graveyard orbits. Colonel Brandon Davenport noted that the constellation was foundational to national defense and protected deployed warfighters from the Gulf War onward. The United States is not left without coverage following this retirement, as the military began launching the more advanced Space Based Infrared System in 2011. Furthermore, the military is currently developing the Next-Generation Overhead Persistent Infrared satellites, with the first of these new spacecraft potentially launching within the next year.

geo.title: FBI arrests a woman accused of spying on Taiwan leader's family for China
geo.excerpt: Federal Bureau of Investigation agents arrested a thirty-four-year-old woman named Wanying Zhang at Los Angeles International Airport as she attempted to board a flight to China. Zhang, also known as Heather, faces charges of acting as an unregistered agent for the Chinese government within the United States. According to Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli, Zhang conducted surveillance on relatives of the Taiwanese president by taking photographs and videos, as well as recording license plate information. Taiwan's Presidential Office confirmed that President Lai Ching-te's relatives were targeted in the operation, labelling the incident as a classic case of transnational repression. Presidential spokesperson Karen Kuo issued a statement condemning the acts as a disregard for human rights and national sovereignty intended to suppress advocates for freedom and democracy. The Chinese Embassy in the United States did not immediately respond to requests for comment, and the Foreign Ministry in Beijing was closed for a holiday. Zhang was scheduled to make an appearance in a federal court in Los Angeles on Monday, while her nationality and legal representation remained unconfirmed. China claims Taiwan as part of its territory following their split after a civil war in 1949, and Beijing regards President Lai as a separatist. Since taking office in 2024, Lai has increased Taiwan's defence spending and promoted new security measures, while maintaining that the People's Republic of China has no right to represent Taiwan.

geo.title: Former Prince Andrew launches challenge to ‘quash’ police search warrants
geo.excerpt: Former British Prince Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has initiated a High Court challenge to quash search warrants obtained by Thames Valley Police prior to his arrest earlier this year. The judiciary confirmed that a London court is scheduled to hold a private hearing on Thursday regarding the legal challenge. The case involves an application by Mountbatten-Windsor for a judicial review to overturn search warrants issued by a judge at the Central Criminal Court on February 18, 2026. Thursday’s upcoming hearing will specifically focus on an application made by Thames Valley Police to restrict access to related court documents. The 66-year-old was arrested on February 19 on suspicion of misconduct in public office following allegations that he shared sensitive information with the late American sex offender Jeffrey Epstein during his tenure as the United Kingdom’s trade envoy. Although he was released later that same day, Mountbatten-Windsor remains under active investigation and has consistently denied any wrongdoing. The police searches in question were conducted at his former homes on royal estates, including his residence on the Sandringham estate in eastern England and the Royal Lodge in Windsor. Mountbatten-Windsor was stripped of his royal titles last year due to his associations with Epstein, who died in a New York prison in August 2019. Thames Valley Police stated that they are engaged in legal proceedings regarding the previously obtained warrants while their investigation into misconduct in public office continues, noting that it would be inappropriate to comment further while legal proceedings remain ongoing.

geo.title: Spanish PM Sánchez calls early election after housing protests
geo.excerpt: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has called an early general election for 29 November following legislative defeats on housing reform. Speculation about a snap poll grew after parliament rejected two government decree laws designed to protect rental tenants. The political pressure intensified following nationwide protests sparked by the eviction of an 87-year-old woman whose rent was increased beyond her pension. In a televised address, Sánchez stated he required a broader progressive majority to push through reforms and overcome elite resistance. His minority left-wing coalition, comprising the Socialist party and the Sumar alliance, was originally not scheduled to face a general election until mid-2027. Sánchez acknowledged mistakes and ongoing problems regarding inequality, public services and housing access during his leadership. In addition to housing challenges, his administration has faced cost-of-living pressures, the Ceuta migration crisis, and several corruption scandals involving his wife, party headquarters, and a former transport minister. Opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo welcomed the announcement as an opportunity for voters to choose change. Opinion polls indicate that the conservative People's Party is likely to win the most seats in the upcoming election, potentially requiring support from the hard-right Vox party to govern.

invest.title: Treasury yields rise to start the week; traders look ahead to Fed minutes
invest.excerpt: United States Treasury yields rebounded on Monday following a sharp decline the previous week, as investors digested fresh economic data and awaited the release of Federal Reserve meeting notes. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield rose by approximately two basis points to 5.298 percent, while the yield on the 30-year bond increased by three basis points to reach 5.659 percent. Conversely, the yield on the 2-year Treasury edged down by nearly one basis point to 4.818 percent. These movements coincided with the publication of new figures from the Institute for Supply Management regarding service sector growth. The report indicated that the Purchasing Manager's Index for the service sector reached 54.9 in September, which aligned with expectations while remaining slightly below the growth rate recorded in August. Additionally, the price index within the service ISM increased by 1.4 points to 74, pushing its twelve-month average to the highest level since March 2023. Market participants are currently focusing on the upcoming publication of the central bank's September policy meeting minutes, which are scheduled for release on Wednesday. Although investors have recently faced a six-week bond market selloff, a weaker-than-expected September jobs report released on Friday helped push yields down and alleviated worries regarding a potential Federal Reserve interest rate hike in October. Consequently, traders are currently pricing in an estimated 82 percent probability that the central bank will maintain its current rates at the upcoming meeting.

invest.title: Jim Cramer's top 10 things to watch in the stock market Monday
invest.excerpt: Stock markets opened flat following a Friday rally fuelled by a soft jobs report that provided the Federal Reserve with justification to keep interest rates steady. The upcoming week features a relatively quiet schedule for corporate news and economic data, though investors await speeches from Fed officials and upcoming central bank meeting minutes. In the oil market, West Texas Intermediate crude traded around ninety dollars a barrel, while Saudi Arabia unexpectedly reduced its official selling prices for Asian buyers. Melius Research upgraded Microsoft to a buy rating with a target of six hundred and sixty-five dollars, pointing to changing narratives surrounding artificial intelligence. Meanwhile, merger and acquisition activity made headlines as Schneider Electric agreed to purchase product design software maker PTC for twenty-two billion dollars. C.H. Robinson also announced plans to acquire truck brokerage RXO for five billion eight hundred million dollars, with Goldman Sachs acting as a financial advisor on the transaction. Elsewhere, Morgan Stanley upgraded Wells Fargo to a buy and named it a top pick, citing a clearer path to profitability following the removal of its asset cap. Bank of America initiated coverage on agricultural spin-off Vylor with a buy rating and a seventy-eight dollar price target. Citi raised its price target on Johnson and Johnson to three hundred and three dollars ahead of upcoming earnings releases. Finally, Barclays reduced its price target for Nike to thirty-seven dollars while maintaining a buy rating as the footwear company trades near thirteen-year lows.
